AM7I-10.solved: 30/15 = 2 h and 30/10 = 3 h, so 60 miles in 5 h; 60/5 = 12 mph.
AM7I-10.note: Genuinely hard by the stated bar: total distance and total time have to be recovered together, and averaging the rates is wrong. 12.5 is the naive (15+10)/2, 5 is the total time, 25 the sum of rates. Best-constructed item in the batch.

AM7I-14.note: 21 = the red count, 7 = one part. Both are what a student actually produces, so the distractors are sound; the item is still one proportion.

AM7I-15.note: Two steps, but strictly sequential in the order the stem states them - no interaction. 200 and 235 are the two half-done answers; 188 = taking the $15 off first.

AM7I-16.solved: Cashews 10 oz, non-cashews 40 oz and that 40 never changes. (10+x)/(50+x) = 1/2 -> 20+2x = 50+x -> x = 30. Check: 40/80 = 50%.
AM7I-16.note: Hard for the right reason: the quantity added changes both numerator and denominator, and the invariant is the part NOT mentioned. 15 = 30% of 50 (treating the change as additive), 25 = half the batch, 10 = the starting cashews.

AM7I-17.note: 15 = 3x5 and 25 = one face are real errors; 60 corresponds to no path I can construct (surface area is 150), so one option is dead.

AM7I-18.note: The stem says dollars, so 6 (the ticket count) is cleanly excluded. 135 = the adult total, 90 = filler.

AM7I-19.note: A rate that changes partway, but the two rates never have to be reconciled - subtract the fixed part, divide by the second rate. Same three-move habit as 18 and 24. 70 = 700/10 ignoring phase one, 58 = 50+8 (total run time).

AM7I-20.note: 48 = tablespoons (unit not converted) and is the trap; 4 and 12 are weaker. Two multiplications in the stated order.

AM7I-21.note: Hard: the two percents compose multiplicatively AND the chain runs backwards, so +20%-15% != +5% and the base differs at each step. 1200 = forgetting the shrink, 850 = applying -15% to the answer, 969 = running the chain forward from 1020.

AM7I-22.solved: Frequencies 2,5,6,8 sum to 21, so the median is the 11th value. Cumulative: 2 students at 0, 7 through 1, 13 through 2. The 11th lies in the 2-sibling group, so the median is 2.
AM7I-22.note: TABLE CHECKED AGAINST ITS OWN LABELS AND IT AGREES. Frequencies 2+5+6+8 = 21, matching both the stem's '21 students' and the caption; the column separators (x=170/209/248/287/328) centre each header over its own frequency, so 0->2, 1->5, 2->6, 3->8 with no off-by-one. 1.95 is the mean (41/21 = 1.952), 3 is the modal value, 1.5 is the median of the four frequencies-as-labels. Good distractors.

AM7I-23.note: Two named statistics, but sequential: recover x by the same mean-recovery move as 05/13/28, then read the middle. 22 = stopping at x, 14 = answering with the mean, 16.5 = averaging the middle pair of four.
